summary: Dedupe bookings by departure date (cheapest hot offer first) to stop the redundant "already booked for that date" rejections seen at d111/d112; core reactive+seasonal-PTO logic unchanged.
describe: Reactive yellowtail strategy. Each tick sums yellowtail (yt) caught fleet-wide over the last 3 fished days, by trip class; a class counts as hot only when that sum is positive, so it cools off within a few skunk days. Offers are booked when their class is hot and bookable (which already reflects budget, PTO and schedule rules), cheapest hot offer first, one booking per departure date, boat is the one that ran that class most in the last 60 days. Because PTO must be committed 14 days before a trip, before any bite signal for that date can exist, PTO for a weekday 14 days out is instead pre-committed from historical day-of-year seasonality, using only seasons since tracking began (an earlier partial record runs far hotter and is dropped as unrepresentative). A day-of-year qualifies only if its historical yellowtail-per-trip rate (+-10 days) clears a floor AND is at least half the best rate found anywhere in the year so far, so scarce PTO goes to the strongest window on record, not the first mediocre one. Weekends, holidays and twilight trips never need PTO and book whenever hot. All actions are skipped quietly on missing data.
